messages:
Maya: Heads up — CI blocked on release/v2.3.1, SAST flagged a keystore usage as hard-coded secret. blocking-pr #4521 :grimacing:
Ben: I looked, scanner couldn't decrypt the build artifact so it fell back to a heuristic and flagged the keystore call site. error from scanner: `kms_decrypt error: PERMISSION_DENIED`
Ben: snippet from pipeline log:
```
> time=2026-03-20T17:02:13Z component=sast-scanner service=scanner-01 msg="kms_decrypt failed" err="projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/keystore: PermissionDenied"
```
Frank: ok — two things: 1) we need the audit entries showing attempted decrypts, 2) don't add a blanket exemption. we should do an ephemeral grant for the scanner service account, capture logs, then revoke.
Alexa: +1. If it is truly a false positive after decrypt, we can add a scoped suppression (repo:infra, rule:SAST-KEystore-001) with owner and TTL. But we need the evidence bundle attached.
sec-bot: Audit log entry found for requestId=ai-98765:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-20T17:02:13Z","principal":"serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com","action":"cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt","resource":"projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/keystore","status":"PERMISSION_DENIED"}
```
Ben: thanks @sec-bot. The service account doesn't have cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on that keyring — I suspect we rotated a key and limited access during rotation.
Liu: we rotated last night as part of keystore hardening, we scoped to only deployer-sa and keystore-ops. scanner-sa was missed.
Maya: decision: grant ephemeral decrypt permission for scanner-sa for 30m, re-run SAST, attach artifact + decrypted contents to triage ticket. No permanent RBAC change until we confirm false positive.
Frank: add steps to run: 1) DevOps-Bot run grant --sa=scanner-sa --key=keystore --role=roles/cloudkms.decrypter --expiry=30m 2) re-run CI 3) collect evidence bundle 4) revoke grant. keep me in loop.
DevOps-Bot: Command received: `grant --sa=scanner-sa --key=keystore --role=roles/cloudkms.decrypter --expiry=30m` — ephemeral grant created, expiry at 2026-03-20T17:32:13Z :white_check_mark:
Ben: re-ran the pipeline, SAST now completed, the keystore usage is normal (constructed via env var and client libs), flagged as FP. evidence attached to triage ticket #SEC-917.
Maya: great — please add the file-level comment in the repo and a short unit test to avoid the heuristic next time. also add a note to the keystore rotation runbook to include scanner-sa allowlist step.
Alexa: I'll prepare the suppression with TTL 7 days and owner=infra-team, and we should schedule a post-mortem sync to discuss RBAC policy for scanners.
Frank: post-mortem agenda: root cause (rotation communication gap), short-term fix (ephemeral grant + suppression), long-term (automated allowlist update in rotation playbook + audit rule to alert if scanners lose decrypt perms). assign owners.
Liu: I'll update the rotation playbook and add a CI check that verifies scanner-sa is in the key ACLs before rotation begins.
Maya: action items in SEC-917: 
- Ben: attach evidence bundle + pipeline logs (done)
- DevOps: revoke ephemeral grant at expiry (or manually after verification)
- Liu: update rotation playbook + add allowlist check
- Alexa: create suppression with TTL and owner
- Frank: follow up on audit alert rule and schedule post-mortem (in 24h)
Ben: quick note — when we did the re-run, I saw an unrelated DAST flaky test. I'll open a separate thread for that so we don't block this release.
Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Frank: leaving a reminder — please don't change key ACLs silently during business hours for Prod without the scanner checklist.
sec-bot: Reminder: ephemeral grant revoked at 2026-03-20T17:32:13Z (revocation verified).
